subject: POC success criteria & KPIs \u0014 next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Alvarez <sara@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: POC success criteria & KPIs  next steps

Hi Sara 

Great to meet earlier today. Thanks for walking through Atlass primary use case and the performance/quality priorities. Per our call, I wanted to capture the proposed success criteria, high-level evaluation plan, owners, and suggested timeline so we have a mutual action plan to move the POC forward. I attached a one-page POC-MAP (see attachment).

Proposed POC success criteria (initial):
- Latency: p95 <= 200 ms (target); p95 <= 220 ms (minimum acceptable) for 12k daily active sessions. p50 target <= 60 ms.
- Throughput: sustain 150 requests/sec during peak trials with 10% headroom for burst traffic.
- Cost: average inference cost <= $0.0008 per token (measured across evaluation workload).
- Quality: intent match / NLU accuracy >= 92% on Atlas intent set; false positive (wrong intent) rate < 3%. No regression > 2% vs baseline on core flows.
- Reliability: uptime >= 99.9% during trial window; graceful fallback to smaller model variant on overload.

Evaluation plan (what we'll measure & how):
1) Baseline capture  Atlas to share a de-identified sample of ~5k representative queries (production logs or synthetic) by EOD Nov 8. Redwood will run this dataset through the candidate model and provide per-query latency, token cost, and quality scoring (intent match).
2) Load run  Redwood to run 3 staged load tests (50%, 100%, 150% of expected peak) during the trial week to validate throughput and SLOs.
3) Quality evaluation  joint review using a 5001,000 labeled holdout set for manual spot checks and automated intent scoring.
4) Acceptance criteria check  documented pass/fail on each KPI at the end of trial week.

Ownership:
- Atlas lead: Sara Alvarez (product/POC contact)
- Redwood implementation lead: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.com)  config, rollout, logging
- Redwood solutions / sales: Jordan Blake  commercial touchpoint & escalation
- Security/compliance: Priya Natarajan (ccd for SOC2 evidence & data handling)

Timeline (proposed):
- Nov 6  POC kickoff call (30m) to finalize test dataset and schedule
- Nov 8  Atlas delivers de-identified dataset and baseline logs
- Nov 1317  Trial execution & load runs
- Nov 20  Review results & acceptance decision

Next steps for this week:
- Sara: confirm dataset delivery timeline and if any additional fields are needed in the sample (PII removed).
- Marissa: prepare canary config and baseline capture instructions (Iccd).
- Jordan: will open the HubSpot MAP and share DocuSign SOW link once dataset delivery date confirmed.

Attachments: POC-MAP.pdf (one-page mutual action plan)

Thanks  happy to adjust the targets if you want to tighten/loosen thresholds based on initial baseline.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Thanks Jordan  this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications: 

1) Dataset: we can provide a de-identified sample of ~6k queries (anonymized) by end of day Nov 8. We'll include metadata fields: intent label, channel, and avg payload size. Attach: data-sample.csv (small subset)
2) Security: we will need SOC2/ISO evidence and confirmation that key logs (request IDs, timestamps) can be retained for 30 days in our tenant. Priya  can you confirm if Redwoods private deployment (VPC) is required for this or if hosted with additional controls suffices?
3) Latency expectations: the 200 ms p95 target is ambitious but sounds achievable if inference is optimized; we may accept up to 220 ms during the run as you suggested.

We also need the SOW for internal procurement  Jordan, could you share the DocuSign link when available?

Happy to proceed on the Nov 6 kickoff.

Sara Alvarez

Subject: RE: POC success criteria & KPIs  next steps

Looping in implementation tasks and owners so we can track in the MAP/HubSpot: 

Action items (Marissa ownership unless noted):
- Marissa: share baseline capture instructions + sample ingestion script by 11/3.
- Priya: share SOC2 evidence checklist and confirm data residency options (hosted w/controls vs Private VPC) by 11/4.
- Jordan: send SOW/DocuSign link and confirm kickoff time on 11/6.
- Marissa + Atlas (Sara): agree on the 5k6k de-identified dataset fields and finalize the holdout labeling plan (target 1k labeled holdout).
- Infra: prepare two model variants for the trial (full model + quantized small variant) and configure automatic fallback.

Measurement details to include in the MAP (definitive KPI definitions):
- Latency: measure end-to-end server-side time excluding network egress; report p50/p95/p99. Acceptance: p95 <= 200 ms target; p95 <= 220 ms acceptable.
- Throughput: concurrency-based test to sustain 150 req/s with <=10% error rate.
- Cost: compute tokenized input+output cost averaged across test queries; acceptance <= $0.0008/token.
- Quality: automated intent-match scoring + manual review sample. Acceptance: >=92% intent match; regression vs baseline <= 2%.

Test plan specifics:
- Baseline pass: Redwood will run the provided dataset on the candidate model within 48 hours of receipt and return a baseline report (latency, cost, intent-match).
- Load testing: schedule three runs during Nov 1317; long-run 60m sustained at target throughput. Logs/metrics will be in the shared Drive folder.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567/ATLAS-4123 and Drive folder linked in the MAP.

I'll prepare the HubSpot MAP entry and invite Sara to the workspace. Anything else to add?

Thanks  Marissa
